summary: Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Patna College, the universities of Lucknow and London, IIT Roorkee, and the Royal School of Mines, before serving in Hyderabad State (~1879–1901) and Cambridge (Reader in Marathi, 1901).
Syed Ameer Ali worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (~1863–1868), where he later held a post from ~1873 to 1878.

Syed Hasan Askari specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University, and later served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali worked in history, archaeology, and related fields. In 1932, he is attested as Principal at Bahauddin College and Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1997), and held a post at Aix-Marseille University around 1999.

Sylvain Lévi worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the EPHE (from 1885), the University of Paris (1889), the Collège de France (1894–1935), and the Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

Sylvie Hureau specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She served as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sze-bong Tso worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gabor College, the University of Göttingen, and under several teachers, later serving as sub-librarian (1831) and Librarian (1837–1841) at The Asiatic Society.
Søren Sørensen worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from ~1887 to 1902.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Nyanaponika Thera.
Sōgen Asahina worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nihon University and held a post at Kanagawa University.

T. Chandrasekharan worked in Indology, studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.

T. Griffith Foulk worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, teaching there (~1987–1995) and at Sarah Lawrence College (attested ~1995–2015).
T. K. V. Desikachar worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1961 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. R. Chintamani worked in Indology after studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951) and as Manager and Correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research.

T. R. V. Murti specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later holding professorships there (~1953–1967), Oxford (~1949–1950), and McMaster University (~1970–1972).
T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held academic posts, including Professor, at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute between 1972 and 1992.
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indologist who held positions at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as a Pandit (attested 1993) and Professor (attested 2026).
